title: The Valley of Jehoshaphat
lead: The place where, in Joel 3, the LORD gathers all the nations for judgment. The name means "the LORD judges"; it is read as a symbolic name, as a real valley near Jerusalem, and as the site of the last judgment.

sections.b: Joel 3:2 and 3:12 name the Valley of Jehoshaphat as the place where the nations are judged; 3:14 calls it the valley of decision. No valley of that name is found elsewhere in the Bible. The nearest narrative is 2 Chronicles 20, where King Jehoshaphat's army wins at the Valley of Beracah ("blessing") without fighting.

From about the fourth century AD, Christian pilgrims (the Bordeaux Pilgrim, AD 333, is the earliest) called the Kidron Valley east of Jerusalem "the Valley of Jehoshaphat", and Jews, Christians and Muslims have buried their dead on its slopes near the Mount of Olives in hope of being near the judgment. The identification is a tradition, not a result of the text.
